mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates active monetary easing, reducing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation requiring aggressive monetary tightening, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where CPIAUCSL 12-month change exceeds 3.5%, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month increase in both housing starts (HOUST) and real consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 0.5% each signals robust consumer demand, accelerating corporate revenue growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where both HOUST and RSAFS rise > 0.5% in 3 months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.5%), a monthly decline in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2 percentage points signals improving labor market conditions, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where UNRATE > 5.5% and declines > 0.2pp in 1 month, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) over the past 3 months indicates expanding manufacturing output, correlating with stronger corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where INDPRO rises for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 800.0 thousand units per month, it signals strong residential construction activity driving economic growth and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where HOUST > 800.0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime (CPIAUCSL 12-month change > 3.5%), a monthly increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25 percentage points signals aggressive monetary tightening, compressing equity valuations and generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL 12-month change > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods where CPIAUCSL 12-month change > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp in 1 month, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly job gains exceed 200.0 thousand (PAYEMS > 200.0), it signals a robust labor market boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods where PAYEMS > 200.0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.
